title: Canonical scalar-association and transition arrows on cochain sheaves
statement: Use the ringed cochain presentations [def-pur-cochain-tensor-coherence-data], module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and the actual sheafified scalar extension [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Scalar extension is the existing construction on objects and maps, with the unique adjunction to scalar restriction whose unit is x mapped to the sheafification of 1 tensor x. Its cochain epsilon is the normalized tensor comparison for the identity geometric morphism. A compatible coefficient square records R to Rprime, S to Sprime, the induced inverse-image ring map and equality of the two maps to Sprime, retaining the same geometric inverse image. Kappa is the unique natural scalar-association isomorphism normalized on every generalized generator by 1 tensor (x tensor 1) mapped to (1 tensor x) tensor 1; linearity and balancing specify all scalars. Tau is the scalar-extension unit followed by restricted inverse kappa, with target restricted from Sprime to S. The restriction tensor map is the adjunction mate of epsilon followed by the two counits, totalled over all bidegrees. IsCompatibleWithCoefficients is the coefficient square containing kappa, epsilon, epsilonS and both pullback tensor comparisons, and the transition square containing tau and the canonical restriction tensor map. Specializing the transition square at every quotient map of a coefficient tower is commutation with all transitions, with no inverse asserted.
